text: Θαρά (Hebr.), Thara, Terah, the father of Abraham.
gloss: Thara, Terah, the father of Abraham

text: θαρρέω, I am courageous, I am of good cheer, a by-form of θαρσέω.
gloss: I am courageous, I am of good cheer

text: θαρσέω, only in the imperative, be of good cheer, a by-form of θαρρέω.
θάρσος, courage.
θαῦμα, (a) concr., a marvel, a wonder; (b) abstr., wonder.
θαυμάσιος, wonderful.
θαυμαστός, to be wondered at, wonderful.
θεά, a goddess.
θεατρίζω, I make a public show of, I expose to public shame.
gloss: I make a public show of, I expose to public shame

text: θέατρον, (a) a theatre, a semi-circular stone building, generally open to the sky; (b) a spectacle, 1 Cor. iv 9.
gloss: a theatre, a semi-circular stone building

text: θεῖον, brimstone, sulphur.
θεῖος, divine; τὸ θεῖον, the divine, the divine nature, Ac. xvii 29.
θειότης (diuinitas), divinity.
θειώδης, of brimstone, sulphurous.
θέλησις, willing, will.
θεοδίδακτος, taught by the god.
θεομάχος, fighting against the god.
θεόπνευστος, inspired by the god, due to the inspiration of the god.
gloss: inspired by the god, due to the inspiration of the god

text: θεοσέβεια, reverence for the god.
θεοσεβής, devout, religious.
θεοστυγής, hating the god.
θεότης (deitas), deity, godhead.
Θεόφιλος, Theophilus, a friend of Luke of equestrian rank, to whom the Gospel and Acts are dedicated.
gloss: Theophilus, a friend of Luke of equestrian rank

text: θεραπεία, care, attention (Lk. xii 42), especially medical attention (treatment) (Lk. ix 11); hence almost healing (Rev. xxii 2). In Lk. xii 42 may, however, be taken as abstr. for concr. (cf. seruitia), the slaves.
θεράπων, a servant, slave.
θεριστής, a reaper, harvester.
θερμαίνομαι, I warm myself.
θέρμη, heat.
θέρος, summer.
Θεσσαλονικεύς, a man of Thessalonica.
Θεσσαλονίκη, Thessalonica (modern Saloniki), an important city of the Roman province Macedonia.
Θευδᾶς, Theudas, a Jewish pretender of date about 4 B.C., otherwise unknown.
gloss: Theudas, a Jewish pretender of date about 4 B.C.

text: θεωρία (spectaculum), a sight.
θήκη, a scabbard, a sheath.
θηλάζω, (a) I give suck; (b) I suck.
θῆλυς, female.
θήρα, hunting, entrapping.
θηρεύω, I hunt, I seek to catch or entrap.
gloss: I hunt, I seek to catch or entrap

text: θηριομαχέω, I fight with wild beasts (i. e. wild beasts in human form).
θιγγάνω, I touch.
θορυβάζω, I disturb greatly.
θορυβέω, I disturb greatly, I terrify, I strike with panic.
gloss: I disturb greatly, I terrify, I strike with panic

text: θόρυβος, (a) din, hubbub, confused noise, Ac. xxi 34, cf. Mk. v 38; (b) riot, disturbance.
θραύω, I crush.
θρέμμα, (lit. a nursling, hence probably) plur. cattle (rather than household, slaves).
θρηνέω, I lament.
θρησκεία (underlying sense, reverence or worship of the gods), worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion.
gloss: worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion

text: θρῆσκος (religiosus) (refers probably to a careful observance of religious restrictions), religious (probably in a limited sense), James i 26.
θριαμβεύω, (properly, I lead one as my prisoner in a triumphal procession, hence) I lead around, I make a show (spectacle) of.
gloss: I lead around, I make a show (spectacle) of

text: θροέω, I disturb, agitate.
θρόμβος, a clot.
Θυάτειρα, Thyatira, a city of the old district Lydia, in the Roman province Asia.
gloss: Thyatira, a city of the old district Lydia

text: θυγάτριον, a little (young) daughter.
θύελλα (procella), a storm, tempest.
θύϊνος, of the sandarach (so-called citron) tree.

θυμιατήριον, (ordinarily censer, but) either the altar of incense (Exod. xxx 1-10), or the shovel, on which the high-priest poured the coals, when he entered the Holy of Holies on the Day of Atonement (Lev. xvi 12).
θυμιάω, I burn incense.
θυμομαχέω, (lit. I fight desperately, hence) I am furiously angry with.
θυμόομαι, I am full of angry passion.
gloss: I am full of angry passion

text: θυρεός (scutum), the heavy oblong Roman shield.
θυρίς, a window-sill.
θυρωρός (ostiarius), door-keeper, porter.
θώραξ, a breastplate, corslet, cuirass.
Ἰάειρος, Jaïrus, a Jewish ruler of the synagogue.
gloss: Jaïrus, a Jewish ruler of the synagogue

text: ἴαμα, a healing, a curing.
Ἰαμβρῆς, Jambres, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh (v. l. Μαμβρῆς).
gloss: Jambres, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh

text: Ἰανναί (Hebr.), Jannai, an ancestor of Jesus, son of Joseph, and father of Melchi.
gloss: Jannai, an ancestor of Jesus, son of Joseph

text: Ἰαννῆς, Jannes, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh (v. l. Ἰαμνῆς).
gloss: Jannes, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh

text: Ἰάρετ (Hebr.), Jareth, son of Maleleel and father of Enoch.
gloss: Jareth, son of Maleleel and father of Enoch

text: ἴασις, healing.
ἴασπις, jasper.
Ἰάσων, Jason, a Christian of Thessalonica, perhaps the same as the ‘relative’ of St. Paul in Rom. xvi 21.
ἰατρός, a physician.
ἰδιώτης, (priuatus, unofficial, hence) an amateur, an unprofessional man, a layman.
gloss: an amateur, an unprofessional man, a layman

text: Ἰδουμαία, Idumaea, Edom, a district of Arabia, immediately S. of Judaea.
gloss: Idumaea, Edom, a district of Arabia

text: ἱδρώς, sweat, perspiration.
Ἰεζάβελ (Zezabel, Old Latin and Armenian), Jezebel, name given to a false prophetess of Thyatira, possibly borrowed from the name of Ahab’s wife, queen of Israel (1 Kings xvi 31, &c.).
gloss: Jezebel, name given to a false prophetess of Thyatira

text: Ἱεράπολις, Hierapolis, a city of the Lycus valley in Phrygia, near Laodicea and Colossae.
gloss: Hierapolis, a city of the Lycus valley in Phrygia

text: ἱερατεία, the duty (office) of a priest.
ἱεράτευμα, act or office of priesthood.
ἱερατεύω, I serve as priest.
Ἰερειχώ (Ἱερειχώ), Jericho, Hiericus, a city a little north of the Dead Sea.
gloss: Jericho, Hiericus, a city a little north of the Dead Sea

text: Ἱερεμίας (Hebr.), Jeremiah, Old Testament prophet (wrote about 603-586 B.C.).
ἱερόθυτος, slain as sacred, slain in sacrifice.
gloss: slain as sacred, slain in sacrifice

text: ἱεροπρεπής, like those employed in sacred service.
gloss: like those employed in sacred service

text: Ἱεροσολυμείτης, an inhabitant of Jerusalem, see Ἱερουσαλήμ.
ἱεροσυλέω, I rob temples.
ἱερόσυλος, a robber of temples, but possibly simply sacrilegious.
ἱερουργέω, I sacrifice.
ἱερωσύνη (earlier ἱερεωσύνη, from ἱερεύς), the abstract notion of the priestly office.
gloss: the abstract notion of the priestly office

text: Ἰεσσαί (Hebr.), Jesse, son of Obed (Iobed), and father of King David.
gloss: Jesse, son of Obed (Iobed), and father of King David

text: Ἰεφθάε (Hebr.), Jephthah, one of the Judges of Israel.
gloss: Jephthah, one of the Judges of Israel

text: Ἰεχονίας (Hebr.), Jechoniah, son of Josiah and father of Salathiel.
gloss: Jechoniah, son of Josiah and father of Salathiel

text: ἱκανότης, sufficiency, ability, power.
ἱκανόω, I make sufficient, I make fit.
gloss: I make sufficient, I make fit

text: ἱκετηρία (originally ἱ. ῥάβδος, the olive branch held in the hand of the suppliant), supplication, entreaty.
ἰκμάς, moisture.
Ἰκόνιον, Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia (mod. Konia).
gloss: Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia

text: ἱλαρός, cheerful.
ἱλαρότης, cheerfulness.
ἱλάσκομαι, (a) c. dat. I have mercy on, I show favour to; (b) tr. with obj. of sins, I forgive.
gloss: I have mercy on, I show favour to

text: ἱλασμός, a propitiation (of an angry god).

ἱλαστήριον (original idea, propitiation of an angry god), (a) a sin offering, by which the wrath of the deity shall be appeased, a means of propitiation, Rom. iii 25; (b) the covering of the ark, which was sprinkled with the atoning blood on the Day of Atonement (Hebr. Kappôreth), Heb. ix 5.
ἵλεως, propitious, forgiving, Heb. viii 12: ἵλεώς σοι = ἵλεως εἴη σοι ὁ θεός, may the god be favourable to you, God be merciful to you, may God help you, God forbid! Mt. xvi 22.
Ἰλλυρικόν, Illyricum, a Roman province, afterwards called Dalmatia, bounded by Pannonia on the N., Macedonia on the S., Moesia on the E., and the Adriatic Sea on the W.
gloss: Illyricum, a Roman province, afterwards called Dalmatia

text: ἱμάς, a thong, strap, (a) for binding a man who is to be flogged, Ac. xxii 25; (b) for fastening a sandal or shoe.
ἱματίζω, I clothe, I provide clothing for.
gloss: I clothe, I provide clothing for

text: ἱματισμός, a collective word, raiment, clothing.
ἰός (cognate with Latin uirus), poison; hence rust, James v 3.
Ἰουδαΐζω, I live as a Jew (in religion, ceremonially).
Ἰουδαϊκός, Jewish, Judaic.
Ἰουδαϊκῶς, in the manner of Jews (religiously, ceremonially).
Ἰουδαϊσμός, the Jewish religion, Judaism.
Ἰουλία, Julia, a Roman Christian, probably a slave or freedwoman of the Imperial household.
Ἰούλιος, Julius, a Roman centurion on special service.
gloss: Julius, a Roman centurion on special service

text: Ἰουνία, Junia, a Roman Christian.

Ἰοῦστος, Justus, (a) a surname of Joseph Barsabbas, one of the two nominated to fill Judas’ place as apostle, Ac. i 23; (b) Titius Justus, a Corinthian Christian, Ac. xviii 7; (c) surname of Jesus, a Christian with St. Paul in Rome.
ἱππεύς, a horse-soldier, a mounted soldier, a cavalryman.
gloss: a horse-soldier, a mounted soldier, a cavalryman

text: ἱππικός, adj. used as collective subst. cavalry.
ἶρις, a rainbow.
ἰσάγγελος, like the angels.
Ἰσκαριώθ, Iscariot, the surname of Judas the Betrayer, which would seem to indicate the place from which he came (v. l. Σκαριώθ).
gloss: Iscariot, the surname of Judas the Betrayer

text: Ἰσκαριώτης, the graecized form of Ἰσκαριώθ, Iscariot (v. l. in John vi 71, xii 4, xiv 22 ἀπὸ Καρυώτου, from Karyotes).
ἴσος (ἶσος), equal, equivalent, identical: τὰ ἴσα, the equivalent, Lk. vi 34; ἴσα, adverbially, on an equality, Phil. ii 6 (if text be sound).
note: accent on the bracketed variant (ἶσος) is faint; read as circumflex with smooth breathing

text: ἰσότης, equality; equality of treatment, fairness.
ἰσότιμος, equally privileged, equal.
ἰσόψυχος, likeminded.
Ἰσραηλείτης (Ἰστραηλείτης), an Israelite, one of the chosen people Israel, a Jew.
gloss: an Israelite, one of the chosen people Israel

text: Ἰσσαχάρ (Hebr.), Issachar, one of the sons of Jacob and founder of a tribe of Israel.
ἱστορέω, I visit, see (some person or object of importance) (rendered ‘inspicio’ in one inscription).
ἴσως, perhaps (cf. Eng. likely).
Ἰταλία, Italy.
Ἰταλικός, Italic, the name of a cohort forming part of the Syrian army.
gloss: Italic, the name of a cohort forming part of the Syrian army

text: Ἰτουραῖος, Ituraean, an adjective applied to a district (χώρα), also called Trachonitic, about 60 miles E. of the Sea of Galilee, and partly inhabited by the nomad tribe called Ituraeans (Ἰτουραῖοι).
ἰχθύδιον, a little fish.
ἴχνος (uestigium), a track, footstep.
Ἰωάθαμ (Hebr.), Joatham, son of Ozias and father of Achaz.
gloss: Joatham, son of Ozias and father of Achaz

text: Ἰωανάν (Hebr.), Joanan, Johanan, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Joanan, Johanan, one of the ancestors of Jesus

text: Ἰώβ (Hebr.), Job, the hero of the Old Testament book of that name.
gloss: Job, the hero of the Old Testament book of that name

text: Ἰωβήδ (Ὠβήδ) (Hebr.), Jobed, Obed, son of Boaz and Ruth, father of Jesse, and grandfather of David.
gloss: Jobed, Obed, son of Boaz and Ruth, father of Jesse

text: Ἰωδά (Hebr.), Jodah, an ancestor of Jesus.
Ἰωνᾶς (Hebr.), Jonah, the Old Testament prophet.
Ἰωράμ (Hebr.), Joram, son of Jehoshaphat and father of Ozias.
gloss: Joram, son of Jehoshaphat and father of Ozias

text: Ἰωρείμ (Hebr.), Jorim, an ancestor of Jesus.
Ἰωσαφάτ (Hebr.), Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, son of Asaph, father of Joram, an ancestor of Jesus.
gloss: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, son of Asaph

text: Ἰωσείας (Hebr.), Josiah, king of Judah, son of Amos and father of Jechoniah.
gloss: Josiah, king of Judah, son of Amos and father of Jechoniah

text: Ἰωσῆς (Hebr.), Joses, son of Mary, sister of Mary, the mother of Jesus; see Ἰωσήφ (d).
gloss: Joses, son of Mary, sister of Mary, the mother of Jesus

text: Ἰωσήχ (Hebr.), Josech, an ancestor of Jesus.
ἰῶτα, yod, the Hebrew or rather Aramaic letter which was smallest of all.
καθά (i. e. καθ’ ἅ, according to which things), as.
καθαίρεσις (destructio), taking down, razing, destroying.
καθαιρέω, (a) I take down, pull down; (b) I depose, Lk. i 52, cf. 2 Cor. x 4, c. gen. I diminish aught from, Ac. xix 27; (c) I destroy, Ac. xiii 19.
καθαίρω, I cleanse, purify.
καθάπτω, I lay hold of, I fasten on to, of a snake with short teeth harmless to the skin.
gloss: I lay hold of, I fasten on to

text: καθαρότης, cleanness.
καθέδρα, a seat, chair.
καθέζομαι, I am sitting, I sit, I am seated.
gloss: I am sitting, I sit, I am seated

text: καθεξῆς (deinceps), in order, in succession: ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς (sc. χρόνῳ), in the time immediately after, just after, Lk. viii 1; οἱ καθεξῆς, those who followed, Ac. iii 24.
καθηγητής, a leader, a teacher.
καθήκω, impers. καθήκει, it is fitting: τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα (a technical phrase of the Stoic philosophy), what is unfitting.
καθημερινός, daily.
καθίημι, I let down.
καθό (i. e. καθ’ ὅ, according to which thing), as, according as.
καθόλου (i. e. καθ’ ὅλου), at all.
καθοπλίζω, tr. I arm completely, I arm cap-à-pie.
gloss: I arm completely, I arm cap-à-pie

text: καθοράω, I see clearly.
καθότι (i. e. καθ’ ὅ, τι [neut. of ὅστις], cf. καθό, καθά), (a) in proportion as, according as, Ac. ii 45, iv 35; (b) because, Lk. i 7, xix 9, Ac. ii 24, xvii 31.
καθώσπερ, according to the very manner in which, even as.
gloss: according to the very manner in which, even as

text: Καϊάφας (Καϊαφᾶς) (Old Latin and Sahidic Καίφας), Caiaphas, Jewish high priest.
Καΐν (Hebr.), Cain, son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
gloss: Cain, son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel

text: Καϊνάμ (Καϊνάν) (Hebr.), Cainam, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
gloss: Cainam, one of the ancestors of Jesus
